# DaVinci AI Commander

> Control DaVinci Resolve with natural language. Type what you want in English or Japanese, and Gemini-powered AI translates intent into Resolve Scripting API calls — bin management, batch rendering, markers, metadata — without writing Python.

## What this is

DaVinci AI Commander is a macOS desktop app that automates the tedious structural parts of DaVinci Resolve post-production. It's safe-by-design: only touches bins, timelines, markers, metadata, and render queues — it cannot modify video content, apply effects, or color grade.

- Platform: macOS 11+ (Big Sur or later)
- Target: DaVinci Resolve 19+ (Free or Studio)
- AI: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash
- Distribution: standalone .app (no Python setup for end users)
- License: see LICENSE in repo

API key storage: macOS Keychain (never plaintext). AI-generated code is validated for dangerous patterns before execution.

## Where to start

- [README](https://github.com/DELAxGithub/davinci-ai-commander/blob/main/README.md) — install, requirements, what it can/cannot do

- Standalone download: `DaVinci-AI-Commander-1.0.0.dmg` in repo releases / root

## What it can do

| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| Bin management | Create, delete, rename bins in bulk |
| Timeline | Create timelines, append clips, read timeline info |
| Markers | Add, list, remove markers with notes |
| Metadata | Read/write clip metadata, project settings |
| Rendering | Queue renders, apply presets, batch export |
| Clip properties | Change clip colors, flags |

## What this is NOT

- Not a video editor — cannot cut, trim, split, or join clips
- Not a color grading tool — cannot apply LUTs, nodes, or grades
- Not a VFX or compositing tool — no effect application
- Not a media analyzer — cannot inspect video/audio content semantically
- Not a Resolve UI macro recorder — operates via the Scripting API, not UI automation

## Requirements

- macOS 11+ • DaVinci Resolve 19+ • Resolve preference "External scripting using" set to **Local** • Google Gemini API key
